transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-03 16:00 UTC | Duration 65m | Attendees: Maya Chen, Ethan Park, Jordan Lee (Redwood) — Priya Singh, Marco Ruiz, Lena Hoffmann, Tom Becker (OptiRetail)

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining — sorry for the slight delay, we had a calendar snafu. i'm Maya, ae on the account. todays, uh, goal is to walk through dedicated vs hosted for your realtime recommender, and dig into runtime perf, kv cache, batching and quantization, and of course security/VPC constraints.

[00:30] Priya Singh: thanks maya. quick context: we run a high-traffic product recommender, p95 latency target 150ms end-to-end, and about 800 qps at peak, with strong tail requirements. privacy and PCI-ish data handling are concerns.

[00:55] Ethan Park: ok good. real quick, can you confirm if the 800 qps is concurrent inference requests or total? and what's average token length for prompts?

[01:10] Priya Singh: average prompt is small, 30 tokens. 800 qps concurrent at holiday peaks, baseline is like 200 qps. we do multi-turn routing but most queries are single-shot.

[01:35] Marco Ruiz: infra constraints: we prefer VPC peering and customer-managed KMS. on-prem is a possibility for cold data but prefer cloud first.

[02:05] Maya Chen: great. i'll hand to ethan to go into runtime and the dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs. ethan?

[02:15] Ethan Park: thanks. so, high level — hosted is our multitenant offering, fastest to get started, auto-scaling, and we have optimizations like prefix KV cache, continuous batching, and quantization variants. Dedicated gives you isolated GPU pools, guaranteed throughput, dedicated autoscaling policies, and the ability to pin model variants and quantization profiles per pool.

[02:45] Lena Hoffmann: when you say guaranteed throughput, is that a hard SLA or more like a target with soft guarantees?

[03:00] Ethan Park: good question. for Dedicated we have SLA-backed throughput tiers for committed capacity — e.g., a reserved pool of n GPUs, with predictable token/sec capacity. it's not per-request hard cap but the pool capacity we commit to is contractual. hosted is best-effort with scaling, but you can face noisy neighbor effects in very high tail scenarios.

[03:30] Priya Singh: noisy neighbor is our main worry — during previous vendor evals we saw spikes that wrecked p95. how does Redwood isolate and mitigate that in hosted?

[03:50] Jordan Lee: in hosted we use request-level smart routing, backpressure, and dynamic throttles. we also maintain per-tenant burst buckets. but because it's multitenant there is some tail variability; we mitigate with automatic fallback to smaller model variants or slower reply modes. For strict isolation you get Dedicated, which avoids co-located tenants on the same GPU nodes.

[04:20] Marco Ruiz: can you explain the quantization story? we need to reduce cost but not break quality for recommendations.

[04:40] Ethan Park: absolutely. we provide model variants: fp16, int8 quantized, and 4-bit profiles. int8 gives 2-3x throughput improvement with modest quality delta; 4-bit often 3-5x but larger risk. we recommend A/B evals on your prompts — Redwood Optimize can run quality regressions against your eval set. in Dedicated you can pin a quant profile so production doesn't flip unexpectedly.

[05:20] Tom Becker: what's the impact of quantization on kv cache and response latency?

[05:35] Ethan Park: quantization mainly affects compute per token and memory. KV cache size reductions are smaller; however int8 models usually reduce memory footprint so larger effective KV cache per GPU which helps for long contexts. latency per token drops because kernels are smaller — but there's a small decode jitter with some quant profiles.

[06:05] Priya Singh: batching — we need low tail latency, so large batching is risky. how does Redwood batch on Dedicated vs Hosted?

[06:25] Ethan Park: we do adaptive batching. Hosted favors slightly more batching to improve unit cost, but you can configure target latency windows. Dedicated gives you more deterministic batching since you control pool sizing and buffer policies. Also, Dedicated pools can be tuned for continuous small batches (low latency) vs large throughput windows.

[07:00] Priya Singh: ok, and KV cache — we heavily rely on prefix caching for session personalization. does the cache live per-GPU and how do you persist or warm it?

[07:20] Jordan Lee: KV cache is in-memory on the serving node/GPU. we support prefix-level cache entries and configurable TTLs. for Dedicated, you can reserve nodes so sessions get sticky routing and keep KV warm; hosted uses LRU and can evict under pressure. we also have a warm-up API to pre-populate cache on start.

[07:55] Marco Ruiz: if cache evicts under hosted, what's the hit on tail latency?

[08:10] Ethan Park: it depends on the cold-start of KV and the model size. for small prompts you might see an extra 50-200ms on first requests; bigger context recompute adds more. Dedicated with sticky routing reduces those evictions significantly.

[08:40] Priya Singh: curious about fallback strategies — can we route to a smaller model variant if the dedicated pool is saturated?

[08:55] Maya Chen: yes, we support policy routing — you can set rules: use Dedicated primary, fallback to hosted compatible model variant (cheap) or queue with graceful degradation. these are configurable per-route.

[09:25] Lena Hoffmann: security: on KMS, how does Redwood integrate? customer-managed keys? audit logs?

[09:40] Jordan Lee: we support customer-managed KMS for Dedicated and Private. for hosted we offer envelope encryption with Redwood-managed key or bring-your-own-key depending on plan. audit logs, per-token tracing and SAML SSO are available; we will share SOC2 docs and our encryption whitepaper.

[10:10] Priya Singh: latency targets: you mentioned 150ms p95 end-to-end — how realistic with your stack?

[10:25] Ethan Park: for 30-token prompts and on Dedicated with tuned batching/kv sticky routing and int8 quant, hitting 80-120ms p95 internal is achievable; end-to-end network and product-side overhead needs to be accounted for. hosted can hit similar medians but tail can be higher due to variability.

[11:00] Marco Ruiz: throughput guarantees: can you give examples of committed pool sizes and expected token/sec?

[11:15] Ethan Park: example — a 8x A100 pool (reserved) with int8 quant on a 7B-ish model yields approx 4k-6k tokens/sec sustained depending on prompt length and batching. we usually run model-specific perf tests — the spreadsheet i'll share has per-model numbers.

[11:50] Tom Becker: networking — for VPC peering, what does the networking hop look like? any observed added latency?

[12:05] Jordan Lee: VPC peering adds a small stable hop, generally 1-10ms depending on region. Private on-prem has larger and more variable network overhead but offers full control.

[12:35] Priya Singh: i want to talk about monitoring and alerting — how do we get token-level cost and latency breakdowns?

[12:50] Maya Chen: Redwood Console shows token-level cost, per-route latency histograms, KV cache hit rates, and batch sizes. for Dedicated you can get more retention and custom dashboards; we also provide tracing hooks for your APM.

[13:20] Marco Ruiz: so if we start hosted and later move to Dedicated, what's the migration effort? any downtime?

[13:35] Ethan Park: migration is usually seamless — same API surface. you'll choose a model variant for Dedicated and pin version; traffic cutover is done via our rollout tooling with canary and automatic fallback. some warm-up steps for KV and batch tuning are recommended but no major code changes.

[14:05] Priya Singh: can we do A/B routing between hosted and dedicated for a subset to compare tail/perf?

[14:20] Maya Chen: yes, we often do canary A/Bs — route 5% to Dedicated and compare p95/p99. Redwood logs and Optimize will run the regression checks.

[14:45] Tom Becker: cost question: what's the rough delta between hosted and Dedicated for our expected load? ballpark numbers?

[15:00] Maya Chen: ballpark — hosted per-token pricing is simpler and may be cheaper at low volume; Dedicated has fixed reserved cost but lower per-token compute cost so at sustained peaks Dedicated tends to be more cost-effective. we'll put numbers in the spreadsheet with assumptions for you.

[15:30] Priya Singh: any gotchas around quantization affecting fairness of recommendations or hallucination rates?

[15:45] Ethan Park: quant can change logits subtly; for recommendation ranking it could shift top-k slightly. we recommend shadow testing and RL-based offline evals. Redwood Optimize can flag quality regressions and rollback profiles automatically.

[16:10] Marco Ruiz: for the benchmark run, what do you need from us?

[16:20] Ethan Park: we'll need a representative request trace or synthetic generator, sample payloads, SLOs (p95, p99 targets), and a preferred model and quant profiles to test. also network egress requirements and KMS config if you want VPC test.

[16:45] Priya Singh: can we run a 24h throughput test that includes holiday peak shape?

[16:55] Ethan Park: yes — we can simulate diurnal patterns and a peak spike. that will show noisy neighbor behavior on hosted vs Dedicated pool behavior.

[17:15] Lena Hoffmann: about compliance — do you support dedicated audit logs per-request for Dedicated?

[17:25] Jordan Lee: yes, per-request audit with retention options. we can show sample logs redacted for PII.

[17:45] Tom Becker: last thing: on-prem — we may want an air-gapped box for PCI tokens, is that realistically possible?

[17:55] Maya Chen: yes, our Private deployment supports on-prem/air-gapped with customer-managed control plane; more effort but it's a path. we'll connect you to the Private team if that's the direction.

[18:20] Maya Chen: ok, quick recap — action items and next steps as we listed: maya to share benchmark spreadsheet and security docs, ethan to provision Dedicated test and run 24h sim, priya to share traces and SLOs, lena to fill security questionnaire. we will schedule follow-up during week of nov 16.

[18:50] Priya Singh: that sounds good — thanks. one small note, we've seen transcription services mangle product names — so pls assume some words may be off in these notes.

[19:05] Maya Chen: noted, thanks. any other questions?

[19:12] Marco Ruiz: no, we're good. thanks everyone.

[19:20] End meeting.

Notes: links referenced: benchmark spreadsheet (link: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/opti-retail-sim), SOC2 whitepaper (link: https://redwood.ai/security/soc2), dedicated pricing worksheet (link: https://redwood.ai/pricing/dedicated).
